prs.title: Async import of the appStore packages

review_comments.body:
### Async forEach callbacks silently discard errors and results **High Severity** The `forEach` callback was changed from synchronous to `async`, but `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the return value of its callback, so the returned promises are silently discarded. In `vital/lib/reschedule.ts` and `wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, this also means the surrounding `try/catch` block can never catch errors from the async operations — they become unhandled promise rejections. Calendar event deletions and video meeting deletions may not complete before the function proceeds. A `for...of` loop with `await` or `Promise.all` with `.map` would be needed instead.
Additional Locations (2) - [`packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts#L124-L134`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-cal_dot_com/blob/e043a5efd872362a3fc146ed0d9ce4393e316c1e/packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts#L124-L134) - [`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx#L552-L567`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-cal_dot_com/blob/e043a5efd872362a3fc146ed0d9ce4393e316c1e/packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx#L552-L567)

### PasswordField visibility toggle broken by type prop override **Medium Severity** Passing `type="password"` to `PasswordField` breaks its show/hide password toggle. `PasswordField` internally manages `type` via `isPasswordVisible` state, but it spreads `{...props}` after its own `type` prop, so the caller's `type="password"` always overrides the internal toggle value. The eye icon button renders and is clickable, but the input never actually switches to `type="text"`. The old code used `TextField` (which has no toggle), so the explicit `type` was needed before but is now harmful with `PasswordField`.

prs.title: fix: handle collective multiple host on destinationCalendar

review_comments.body:
### Fallback calendar lookup always evaluates to undefined **High Severity** In both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, the fallback branch uses `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` — but this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. Comparing `cal.externalId` against a falsy value will never match, so the fallback always returns `undefined`. Previously, it returned the single `destinationCalendar`'s `externalId`. In `updateEvent`, this causes `calendarId` to be `undefined` (passed directly to the API). In `deleteEvent`, it falls through to `"primary"`, but that may be wrong.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts#L314-L317`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-cal_dot_com/blob/bd797c1ea00a61425735f2b9fd7ce212ebf8c8ab/packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts#L314-L317)

### Missing optional chaining causes crash on undefined **High Severity** When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array, destructuring produces `mainHostDestinationCalendar` as `undefined`. Accessing `.integration` on `undefined` without optional chaining throws a `TypeError` at runtime. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` which was safe.

### Organization slug assignment logic is inverted **High Severity** The original code set `slug` directly when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` (billing disabled). The new code sets `slug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true (billing enabled), reversing the logic. When billing is enabled, only `requestedSlug` in metadata was supposed to be set (for later confirmation), not the direct `slug`. Now both `slug` and `requestedSlug` are set when billing is enabled, and neither is set when billing is disabled.

### Dynamic user query drops required organization select **Medium Severity** The refactored `loadUsers` query for dynamic users no longer includes the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` field that was present in the original code. The returned users are cast to `IsFixedAwareUser`, which requires `organization: { slug: string }`. Downstream code relying on `organization.slug` would get `undefined`, potentially breaking organization-aware booking flows.

### Video reference credentialId is always set to undefined **High Severity** For non-calendar (video) results, `credentialId` is now unconditionally set to `undefined`. The old code used `result.credentialId` for video types, which contained the actual credential ID from `createMeeting`. This means video booking references will no longer have a `credentialId`, breaking downstream logic in cancellation flows (e.g., `handleCancelBooking`) that checks `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` to locate the right credential for deleting video meetings.

### Team destination calendars silently dropped when null **Medium Severity** When neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null`. The subsequent `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then becomes a no-op on `null`, silently discarding all team members' destination calendars for collective events. Using `[]` instead of `null` as the fallback would allow the push to succeed.

### Update results lack externalId and credentialId fields **Medium Severity** In `updateLocation`, `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId` are both always `undefined` for calendar update results because `CalendarManager.updateEvent` doesn't include those fields in its return value (unlike `createEvent` which was updated to return them). The old code fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`. Now the booking references created after a location update will lose their `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`, which are needed for future calendar event updates and deletions.

prs.title: feat: convert InsightsBookingService to use Prisma.sql raw queries
Comprehensive workflow reminder management for booking lifecycle events

review_comments.body:
### Rescheduling path inconsistently skips immediate email cancellation **High Severity** `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` in `bookings.tsx` is called without `immediateDelete: true` during rescheduling, while `handleNewBooking.ts` passes `true` for the identical rescheduling scenario. Without `immediateDelete`, the function only marks the reminder as `cancelled` in the DB and defers actual SendGrid cancellation to a cron job. If the cron doesn't run before the scheduled send time, the old reminder email for the previous booking time will still be delivered — potentially alongside the new reminder for the rescheduled time.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts#L966-L968`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-cal_dot_com/blob/2ebfcf448c7e4136ac1b8b9ef9b526a4424fd155/packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts#L966-L968)

### Cancelled booking emails not immediately cancelled in SendGrid **Medium Severity** `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is called without `immediateDelete: true` during booking cancellation. The old code immediately cancelled the SendGrid scheduled send; the new code only marks the DB record as `cancelled` and defers actual SendGrid cancellation to a cron job. If the reminder's scheduled time arrives before the cron processes it, cancelled-booking reminder emails are still delivered to attendees.

### Single SendGrid failure blocks all cron reminder cancellations **Medium Severity** The `try/catch` wraps the entire `for` loop and the `Promise.all` for DB deletions. If any single SendGrid API call fails, the remaining reminders aren't processed, and all already-queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` operations are never executed (since `Promise.all` is skipped). On subsequent cron runs, the same batch is retried — including the failing reminder — creating a potentially permanent block.

### Immediate delete path leaves orphaned reminder DB records **Low Severity** When `immediateDelete` is `true` and `referenceId` is non-null, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` cancels the SendGrid send but returns without deleting or marking the DB record. For callers like `handleNewBooking.ts` (rescheduling), where no cascade delete follows, the `WorkflowReminder` record remains orphaned — not marked `cancelled`, so the cron won't clean it up until its `scheduledDate` passes the initial past-dated cleanup.

prs.title: Advanced date override handling and timezone compatibility improvements

review_comments.body: ### Dayjs object reference comparison always returns false **High Severity** The `===` operator on two `dayjs` objects compares references, not values, so this condition is always `false`. This means when a date override has equal `start` and `end` (representing a day off / unavailable block), the check is silently skipped. Any slot overlapping that override time will incorrectly be marked as available via the `dateOverrideExist` path, instead of being blocked. The comparison needs to use `dayjs`'s `.isSame()` method.

### Slot end time variable uses start time instead **High Severity** The `end` variable is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, making it identical to `start`. The check `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore only validates the slot's start time against the working hour boundary, not its end. Slots that begin within working hours but extend past them won't be filtered out, allowing bookings that overflow past the organizer's availability window.

### Working hours check rejects slots valid in split schedules **High Severity** The working hours check uses `find` to locate any working hour range where the slot falls outside, then marks the slot unavailable. But a user can have multiple working hour ranges on the same day (e.g., 9–12 and 13–17 for a lunch break, or from timezone overflow). A slot at 10 AM would be rejected because it's outside the 13–17 range, even though it's inside the 9–12 range. The logic needs to verify the slot is outside *all* applicable ranges before marking it unavailable, not just that it's outside *any* single one.

prs.title: OAuth credential sync and app integration enhancements

review_comments.body:
### Google Calendar stores safeParse wrapper instead of credential data **High Severity** `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `safeParse` result object (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), but here it's stored directly as `key` in the database. The previous code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse()` which returns just the data. Every other caller (Office365, Zoom, Salesforce) correctly accesses `.data` from the result, but Google Calendar does not. This corrupts the stored credential, and subsequent reads via `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will fail because the shape no longer matches.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts#L28-L29`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-cal_dot_com/blob/824145b0e245661875240ed5c8745decd2293d1a/packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts#L28-L29)

### Zoho Bigin passes credential ID instead of user ID **Medium Severity** The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (which is `credential.id`), but the parameter expects a `userId`. Every other integration (Google, HubSpot, Lark, Office365, Webex, Zoom, Zoho CRM) correctly passes `credential.userId`. When credential sharing is enabled, this sends the wrong ID as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint.

### Schema uses nonsensical computed property names from Zod **Medium Severity** `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed property names `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to literal string representations of Zod type objects (e.g., `"ZodString"`), not dynamic key validators. This creates a schema requiring nonsensical literal property names, causing `safeParse` to fail on any real API response when credential sharing is enabled.

### Salesforce connection uses old token after refresh **Medium Severity** The new code proactively refreshes the Salesforce access token and stores the updated token in the DB via `accessTokenParsed.data`, but the `jsforce.Connection` is still created with the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url`. The refreshed `access_token` and potentially updated `instance_url` from `accessTokenParsed.data` are never passed to the connection, making the refresh ineffective for the current session.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts#L74-L99`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-cal_dot_com/blob/824145b0e245661875240ed5c8745decd2293d1a/packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts#L74-L99)

### HubSpot treats fetch Response as HubspotToken type **Medium Severity** When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object, but the HubSpot code assigns it as `HubspotToken`. Accessing `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` on a `Response` yields `undefined`, producing `NaN` for `expiryDate` and passing `undefined` to `setAccessToken`. The corrupted object is then stored in the database.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts#L4-L15`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-cal_dot_com/blob/824145b0e245661875240ed5c8745decd2293d1a/packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts#L4-L15)

prs.title: SMS workflow reminder retry count tracking

review_comments.body: ### Unscoped retryCount delete affects non-SMS workflow reminders **High Severity** The second branch of the `OR` condition in `deleteMany` filters only on `retryCount > 1` without also filtering on `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. This causes the query to delete **all** `WorkflowReminder` records (including `EMAIL` and `WHATSAPP` reminders) that have `retryCount > 1`, not just SMS ones. The `method` constraint needs to be added to the `retryCount` branch to scope deletions to SMS reminders only.

### Throwing await in catch block aborts reminder loop **Medium Severity** The `catch` block now contains an `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` call that is not itself wrapped in a try-catch. If this database call fails (e.g., transient DB connectivity issue — the same kind of error that may have triggered the catch), the exception propagates unhandled, aborting the `for` loop and preventing all subsequent reminders from being processed. Previously, the catch block only called `console.log`, which could never throw, guaranteeing the loop always continued.

prs.title: Add guest management functionality to existing bookings

review_comments.body: ### Authorization check uses AND instead of OR **High Severity** The `isTeamAdminOrOwner` variable uses `&&` (AND) but the intent (per the variable name) is `||` (OR). Since `isTeamAdmin` matches ADMIN or OWNER roles while `isTeamOwner` matches only OWNER, using `&&` effectively restricts access to team owners only — team admins who aren't owners are incorrectly denied permission to add guests.

### Wrong guest list passed to email function **Medium Severity** `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`. The email function uses `newGuests` to decide email type — if an already-existing attendee's email is in `guests`, they'll incorrectly receive an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (full booking confirmation) instead of an `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (guest-added notification). Passing `uniqueGuests` would fix the email routing logic.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/emails/email-manager.ts#L538-L546`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-cal_dot_com/blob/baa9045af7711ea0b86390cb0bf0fdce5430228c/packages/emails/email-manager.ts#L538-L546)

### Blacklist email check is case-sensitive while list is lowercased **Low Severity** The `blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased, but the `guest` emails in the filter comparison are not lowercased before calling `includes`. A guest email with mixed or uppercase characters (e.g., `Spam@Test.com`) would bypass the blacklist check despite being listed.

### Stale validation error persists across dialog sessions **Medium Severity** The `isInvalidEmail` state is never reset to `false` when validation succeeds in `handleAdd` or when the mutation succeeds in `onSuccess`. The cancel handler resets it, but the success paths don't. If a user triggers a validation error, then fixes their input and submits successfully, the error banner remains visible during the mutation and reappears when the dialog is reopened (since the component stays mounted).
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx#L47-L58`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-cal_dot_com/blob/baa9045af7711ea0b86390cb0bf0fdce5430228c/apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx#L47-L58)

### Error toast fallback message is unreachable **Low Severity** The `message` variable is a template literal (`` `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` ``), which always produces a non-empty string — even when `err.data` is undefined, it yields `"undefined: ..."`. Since a non-empty string is truthy, the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback in `showToast` can never be reached. Users would see `"undefined: ..."` in the error toast instead of the intended friendly fallback message.

prs.title: feat: add calendar cache status and actions (#22532)

review_comments.body: ### Date formatting ignores user locale, hardcodes English **Medium Severity** The `Intl.DateTimeFormat` constructor is hardcoded to `"en-US"` instead of using the user's locale from `i18n.language`. The `useLocale()` hook is already imported and used in this file but only `t` is destructured — `i18n` is available but unused. The rest of the codebase consistently passes `i18n.language` to `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (e.g., in `Header.tsx` and `dates.tsx`). Non-English users will see US-formatted dates in the cache status dropdown.

### Empty wrapper div always rendered when dropdown returns null **Low Severity** The `actions` prop now always receives a `
` wrapper, but `CredentialActionsDropdown` returns `null` when there are no available actions. Previously, `actions` was `false` when conditions weren't met. The `Alert` component checks `props.actions && (...)` to conditionally render an actions container — a truthy empty div now always triggers that container. Similarly, `AppListCard` renders `{actions}` directly, so the empty 128px-wide div consumes space in the flex row. This causes a layout regression for delegation credentials on non-Google calendars, where no actions exist but an empty space is reserved.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/platform/atoms/selected-calendars/wrappers/SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx#L122-L132`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-cal_dot_com/blob/cb7869234729f908648af6796ab4082b569daf39/packages/platform/atoms/selected-calendars/wrappers/SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx#L122-L132)
